traceability.evidence:
Story file exists: docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md.
Rule implementations: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts defines ESLint rule `require-story-annotation` (RuleModule) with meta, messages, schema and create(context). It imports shared helpers from ./helpers/require-story-visitors and ./helpers/require-story-helpers and is annotated with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts defines ESLint rule `require-req-annotation` (RuleModule) with meta, messages, schema and create(context). It imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from ./helpers/require-story-helpers and checkReqAnnotation from ../utils/annotation-checker, and is annotated with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md.
Shared function detection and scope (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts defines DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration","FunctionExpression","MethodDefinition","TSMethodSignature","TSDeclareFunction"] and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all","exported","non-exported"]. Arrow functions are not part of DEFAULT_SCOPE. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts implements shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) which filters nodes by type and export status using isExportedNode(). It is used by both rules (directly in require-req-annotation and via options.shouldProcessNode in require-story-visitors). - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts builds visitors for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, and ArrowFunctionExpression. All visitors call options.shouldProcessNode(node) before reporting. Because DEFAULT_SCOPE excludes "ArrowFunctionExpression", arrow functions are ignored by default, matching the story requirement that arrow functions are excluded. - require-req-annotation.create() uses the same DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES and shouldProcessNode logic as require-story-annotation, so both rules enforce their annotations on the same function-like constructs with identical scope and exportPriority semantics. - TypeScript support: require-story-visitors.ts adds TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature visitors for @story; require-req-annotation.ts has TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature listeners that call runCheck(node); annotation-checker.ts includes TS-oriented heuristics via sourceCode, lines, ranges and parent chain.
JSDoc/comment parsing and robust detection (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and @req detection): - For @story (require-story-annotation): src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts defines jsdocHasStory(), commentsBeforeHasStory(), leadingCommentsHasStory(), and hasStoryAnnotation() which combines these with imported helpers linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory. hasStoryAnnotation() wraps all checks in try/catch to avoid crashing on malformed comments or source. - For @req (require-req-annotation): src/utils/annotation-checker.ts defines getJsdocComment(), getLeadingComments(), getCommentsBefore(), combineComments(), commentContainsReq(), and the heuristics linesBeforeHasReq(), parentChainHasReq(), fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(), and hasReqAnnotation(). hasReqAnnotation() uses the same pattern: advanced heuristics first (with try/catch) then falls back to checking JSDoc and combined comments for "@req". checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options) wires this detection into the rule, calling reportMissing when !hasReq.
Annotations required & same construct set (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, Core Functionality AC): - require-story-annotation: src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts defines visitors for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (excluding MethodDefinition parents), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. Each visitor checks options.shouldProcessNode(node) then calls helperReportMissing or helperReportMethod from require-story-helpers, which use hasStoryAnnotation() and context.report() with messageId "missingStory". This enforces @story on all in-scope function-like constructs. - require-req-annotation: src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts create() builds shouldCheck(node) via shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority). For FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (excluding MethodDefinition parents), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, it calls runCheck(node) which invokes checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }). This enforces @req on the same function-like constructs, with identical scoping and exportPriority rules. - Because both rules share DEFAULT_SCOPE and shouldProcessNode(), they apply to the same set of constructs and configuration, satisfying the requirement that they enforce @story and @req together on the same functions when both rules are enabled.
Error location & user experience (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, User Experience AC): - require-story-annotation: require-story-helpers.ts reportMissing() computes functionName via extractName() and sets nameNode to the function/method identifier (node.id or node.key) when available. It then calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createAddStoryFix(...), suggest: [...] }). reportMethod() does the same for MethodDefinition/TSMethodSignature, using node.key as the anchor. This ensures errors are located at the function name or method name as specified. - require-req-annotation: annotation-checker.ts reportMissing() obtains a readable name from getNodeName(node) or parent, assembles nameNode as node.id or node.key when Identifier, and calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingReq", data: { name, functionName: name }, ... }). Messages defined in src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts include explicit guidance and examples: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE')...". This provides clear, actionable error messages.
Error handling / malformed cases (Error Handling AC): - hasStoryAnnotation() wraps all detection in try/catch and returns false on any exception (comments or source issues), so the rule degrades gracefully rather than throwing. - hasReqAnnotation() in annotation-checker.ts similarly wraps advanced heuristics in try/catch, and comments explicitly state it treats IO/detection failures as "no annotation" instead of throwing. Detection helpers validate inputs (loc, range) before use and return false when data is missing or malformed.
Documentation (Documentation AC): - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md: documents the rule, references @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md, lists supported node types (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), fully documents options (scope and exportPriority) including JSON schema, defaults, configuration example, and JS/TS examples of correct and incorrect usage. - docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md: documents the rule, references the same story, lists the supported constructs (function declarations, expressions, methods, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), explicitly states arrow functions are not checked, and documents options (scope, exportPriority) mirroring require-story-annotation. It includes multiple JS and TS examples showing correct and incorrect @req usage.
Tests and explicit linkage to story (Definition-of-Done: tests & traceability): - Jest config: jest.config.js has a JSDoc header with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and configures tests under tests/**/*.test.ts using ts-jest, ensuring TypeScript rule tests are supported. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - File header: "Tests for: docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md" plus @story and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Uses ESLint RuleTester with JS and TS parserOptions. - Valid tests cover: function declarations with JSDoc @story, line comment @story, function expressions, arrow functions with @story, class methods, TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with @story, and an unannotated arrow function which is allowed by default. - Invalid tests cover missing @story on: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. Each asserts messageId: "missingStory", correct suggestion descriptions, and correct autofix output, including exportPriority and scope options. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - File header: @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md with @req tags describing required behavior. - Valid tests: functions with only @req, with both @story and @req, TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with @req, JS and TS function expressions and methods with @req, plus scope/exportPriority configurations ("exported", "non-exported") demonstrating correct inclusion/exclusion. - Invalid tests: missing @req on function declarations (with and without @story), TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, function expressions (including anonymous and IIFEs), class and object methods, and various scope/exportPriority scenarios. All assert messageId "missingReq" and data { name, functionName } for precise error context.

traceability.notes: The story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented. Both ESLint rules `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` exist, share a common detection and scoping model (DEFAULT_SCOPE, exportPriority, shouldProcessNode), and cover FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, and TSMethodSignature while excluding arrow functions by default. JSDoc and surrounding comment parsing is implemented for both @story and @req using robust helper functions with defensive error handling. Errors are reported at the function or method name with clear, actionable messages and suggested fixes, and both rules support TypeScript syntax and decorators via @typescript-eslint/parser and TS node visitors. Documentation for each rule is present with examples and configuration options, and comprehensive RuleTester-based Jest tests in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts explicitly reference this story and validate the required behavior, scope, and exportPriority options. A targeted Jest run for these tests executes without reported failures. Based on this concrete evidence, all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for this story are satisfied.
